blocks.text: Śiva Sūtras 3.41
blocks.directed: [long pause] Śiva Sūtras 3.41

blocks.text: तदारूढप्रमितेस्तत्क्षयाज्जीवसङ्क्षयः
blocks.directed: [slowly] तदारूढप्रमितेस्तत्क्षयाज्जीवसङ्क्षयः

blocks.text: Tadārūḍhapramites tatkṣayāj jīvasaṅkṣayaḥ.
blocks.directed: Tadārūḍhapramites tatkṣayāj jīvasaṅkṣayaḥ.

blocks.text: For one whose awareness is established in that supreme state, the ending of desire brings the dissolution of conditioned individuality.
blocks.directed: For one whose awareness is established in that supreme state, the ending of desire brings the dissolution of conditioned individuality.

blocks.text: Your Limited Self Has Been Cancelled. Nobody Actually Died.
blocks.directed: Your Limited Self Has Been Cancelled. Nobody Actually Died.

blocks.text: Now this is absolutely central to the ending of the entire Śiva Sūtras.
blocks.directed: Now this is absolutely central to the ending of the entire Śiva Sūtras.

blocks.text: Let’s unpack it carefully.
blocks.directed: Let’s unpack it carefully.

blocks.text: Tad — that; referring to the supreme condition of turya.
blocks.directed: Tad — that; referring to the supreme condition of turya.

blocks.text: Ārūḍha — ascended to, established in.
blocks.directed: Ārūḍha — ascended to, established in.

blocks.text: Pramiti — knowledge, conscious apprehension.
blocks.directed: Pramiti — knowledge, conscious apprehension.

blocks.text: Tat-kṣayāt — through the destruction of that; referring back to desire.
blocks.directed: Tat-kṣayāt — through the destruction of that; referring back to desire.

blocks.text: Jīva — the living, conditioned individual.
blocks.directed: Jīva — the living, conditioned individual.

blocks.text: Saṅkṣayaḥ — complete dissolution, cessation, exhaustion.
blocks.directed: Saṅkṣayaḥ — complete dissolution, cessation, exhaustion.

blocks.text: Now, Kṣemarāja explicitly explains both instances of tad.
blocks.directed: Now, Kṣemarāja explicitly explains both instances of tad.

blocks.text: The first refers to the supreme conscious state.
blocks.directed: The first refers to the supreme conscious state.

blocks.text: The second refers to the desire described in 3.40.
blocks.directed: The second refers to the desire described in 3.40.

blocks.text: So the sequence is:
blocks.directed: [short pause] So the sequence is:

blocks.text: Awareness becomes established in the supreme reality.
blocks.directed: Awareness becomes established in the supreme reality.

blocks.text: The fundamental craving arising from incompleteness subsides.
blocks.directed: The fundamental craving arising from incompleteness subsides.

blocks.text: And the limited condition of the jīva comes to an end.
blocks.directed: And the limited condition of the jīva comes to an end.

blocks.text: But here’s the crucial question.
blocks.directed: But here’s the crucial question.

blocks.text: What exactly is being destroyed?
blocks.directed: What exactly is being destroyed?

blocks.text: Not the physical body.
blocks.directed: Not the physical body.

blocks.text: Not the existence of consciousness.
blocks.directed: Not the existence of consciousness.

blocks.text: Not the possibility of ordinary experience.
blocks.directed: Not the possibility of ordinary experience.

blocks.text: What ceases is the identification of the Self with the limited puryaṣṭaka as the ultimate knowing subject.
blocks.directed: What ceases is the identification of the Self with the limited puryaṣṭaka as the ultimate knowing subject.

blocks.text: That is Kṣemarāja’s explanation.
blocks.directed: That is Kṣemarāja’s explanation.

blocks.text: The jīva as the contracted, desire-driven individual ceases to define the Self.
blocks.directed: The jīva as the contracted, desire-driven individual ceases to define the Self.

blocks.text: And now we encounter an absolutely beautiful expression.
blocks.directed: And now we encounter an absolutely beautiful expression.

blocks.text: Ātmārāmatā.
blocks.directed: [slowly] Ātmārāmatā.

blocks.text: Delight in one’s own Self.
blocks.directed: Delight in one’s own Self.

blocks.text: Resting in the fullness of the Self.
blocks.directed: Resting in the fullness of the Self.

blocks.text: The person no longer requires an external object to establish their fundamental completeness.
blocks.directed: The person no longer requires an external object to establish their fundamental completeness.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja contrasts this with the continual outward movement of the bound individual.
blocks.directed: And Kṣemarāja contrasts this with the continual outward movement of the bound individual.

blocks.text: Now, something fascinating happens.
blocks.directed: Now, something fascinating happens.

blocks.text: He cites a tantric passage comparing liberation to waking from a dream.
blocks.directed: He cites a tantric passage comparing liberation to waking from a dream.

blocks.text: When you awaken, the objects of the dream are no longer experienced as the actual environment in which you’re situated.
blocks.directed: When you awaken, the objects of the dream are no longer experienced as the actual environment in which you’re situated.

blocks.text: The dream city.
blocks.directed: The dream city.

blocks.text: The dream characters.
blocks.directed: The dream characters.

blocks.text: The dream catastrophe.
blocks.directed: The dream catastrophe.

blocks.text: Their former apparent authority is withdrawn.
blocks.directed: Their former apparent authority is withdrawn.

blocks.text: And similarly, the yogi who recognises the supreme reality no longer apprehends saṃsāra through the same fundamental delusion.
blocks.directed: And similarly, the yogi who recognises the supreme reality no longer apprehends saṃsāra through the same fundamental delusion.

blocks.text: But this doesn’t mean that the physical universe disappears for everyone else.
blocks.directed: But this doesn’t mean that the physical universe disappears for everyone else.

blocks.text: Nor that the enlightened person ceases to perceive ordinary objects.
blocks.directed: Nor that the enlightened person ceases to perceive ordinary objects.

blocks.text: The analogy concerns the transformation of their conscious standpoint.
blocks.directed: The analogy concerns the transformation of their conscious standpoint.

blocks.text: The world is no longer experienced as a realm fundamentally separate from Śiva.
blocks.directed: The world is no longer experienced as a realm fundamentally separate from Śiva.

blocks.text: And here’s a remarkable detail.
blocks.directed: And here’s a remarkable detail.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja’s cited material actually uses the term nirvāṇa.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja’s cited material actually uses the term nirvāṇa.

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.directed: [short pause] Yes.

blocks.text: Nirvāṇapada.
blocks.directed: [slowly] Nirvāṇapada.

blocks.text: The state of nirvāṇa.
blocks.directed: The state of nirvāṇa.

blocks.text: Now, we should not automatically equate this with the Buddhist understanding of Nibbāna.
blocks.directed: Now, we should not automatically equate this with the Buddhist understanding of Nibbāna.

blocks.text: The metaphysical frameworks are substantially different.
blocks.directed: The metaphysical frameworks are substantially different.

blocks.text: In the Buddhist traditions, nirvāṇa is associated with the cessation of greed, hatred and delusion, without positing an eternal universal Śiva-self.
blocks.directed: In the Buddhist traditions, nirvāṇa is associated with the cessation of greed, hatred and delusion, without positing an eternal universal Śiva-self.

blocks.text: In Trika, Kṣemarāja interprets liberation through recognition of the supreme conscious Self, inseparable from divine freedom and Śakti.
blocks.directed: In Trika, Kṣemarāja interprets liberation through recognition of the supreme conscious Self, inseparable from divine freedom and Śakti.

blocks.text: The resemblance in vocabulary is real.
blocks.directed: The resemblance in vocabulary is real.

blocks.text: But so is the philosophical difference.
blocks.directed: But so is the philosophical difference.

blocks.text: And this is an excellent example of why we need to read the actual Sanskrit rather than assuming a word has exactly the same meaning everywhere.
blocks.directed: And this is an excellent example of why we need to read the actual Sanskrit rather than assuming a word has exactly the same meaning everywhere.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja describes the yogi as established in kaivalya because they are no longer carried along by the senses and subtle elements.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja describes the yogi as established in kaivalya because they are no longer carried along by the senses and subtle elements.

blocks.text: The individual no longer remains a helpless passenger within the machinery of conditioned existence. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: The individual no longer remains a helpless passenger within the machinery of conditioned existence. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.

blocks.text: Now here’s the extraordinary result.
blocks.directed: Now here’s the extraordinary result.

blocks.text: The body may continue.
blocks.directed: The body may continue.

blocks.text: The senses may function.
blocks.directed: The senses may function.

blocks.text: The world may appear.
blocks.directed: The world may appear.

blocks.text: But the fundamental sense of being an incomplete individual driven outward by desire has been overcome.
blocks.directed: But the fundamental sense of being an incomplete individual driven outward by desire has been overcome.

blocks.text: And this takes us to one of the most beautiful metaphysical corrections in the entire work.
blocks.directed: And this takes us to one of the most beautiful metaphysical corrections in the entire work.

blocks.text: Because if the jīva has been dissolved, why is the liberated person still walking around?
blocks.directed: Because if the jīva has been dissolved, why is the liberated person still walking around?

blocks.text: Surely their body should vanish?
blocks.directed: Surely their body should vanish?

blocks.text: Shouldn’t they immediately ascend into some luminous cosmic dimension?
blocks.directed: Shouldn’t they immediately ascend into some luminous cosmic dimension?

blocks.text: Well.
blocks.directed: Well.

blocks.text: Vasugupta has thought of that.
blocks.directed: Vasugupta has thought of that.

blocks.text: And the answer is wonderful.
blocks.directed: And the answer is wonderful.

blocks.text: The body remains like a cloak.
blocks.directed: The body remains like a cloak.
